editorial.evidence: 16 November 2026: read all 46 captured sections (about 19,000 words) of the workflow-orchestration source and wrote the casebook from scratch. The brief opens on the six-system process and the irreversible payment, defines workflow, activity, side effect, business-level exactly once, idempotency key, compensation, saga and durable history before use, and adds an o-123 example taken from the source's own code and tests. Tutorial parts 1-4, 6 and 7 became walkthrough steps 1-8; part 5's records, code and tests, the retry formula, the four trade-offs and the coverage-notes gap essays moved to deep dives, with source section numbers replaced by links. Bullet-list source material was rewritten as connected prose, and list-shaped data (question tree, must/should/could, scorecard, phases, risk register, 50-minute plan) became tables. All three code blocks and all 14 figure pairs are kept beside their explanations; of the ten source tables, seven are reproduced, the two blank worksheet templates became prompts with authored worked answers, and the old sections table became reading guidance. Additions are labelled: an illustrative backoff schedule, the o-123 traces, two authored worksheet answers, an implementation trace, and caveats that the test fixtures are undefined and the no-double-charge sketch does not prove durability. Repeated sentences (the history/receipt rule, retry-storm partitioning, the outcome line) were consolidated where they repeat. No source item was omitted.
